claims.claim: Genentech advanced the collaboration's first neuroscience target into a joint early-discovery program, a concrete external-partner validation step for Recursion's target-discovery platform.
REC-7735 had an IND cleared and was expected to start Phase 1/2 in 2H26 after being designed to exceed 100-fold mutant selectivity.

factors.name: partner validation
factors.basis: A named Genentech target moved into a joint program.

factors.name: clinical translation
factors.basis: IND clearance advances platform output toward human testing, but efficacy remains unproven.

risks.risk: Platform validation does not establish clinical efficacy or commercial success.

unknowns.unknown: REC-7735 trial initiation and subsequent human data after the August update require later verification.

claims.claim: At June 30 Recursion reported $556.8M cash/cash equivalents/restricted cash and expected runway into early 2028 without additional financing.
Q2 revenue was $7.7M versus $19.2M a year earlier while net loss narrowed to $131.0M from $171.9M; 2026 cash operating expense guidance was reduced to below $375M.

factors.name: runway
factors.basis: Management maintained early-2028 runway while lowering cash operating expense guidance.

factors.name: revenue dependence
factors.basis: Collaboration revenue declined materially year over year and remains milestone-sensitive.

risks.risk: Cash burn and clinical-development uncertainty remain substantial before product economics are proven.

unknowns.unknown: No Scout valuation or entry-price conclusion is asserted.
